items.title: Identifying and fixing performance bottlenecks (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of Identifying and fixing performance bottlenecks (PDF 70-72, printed 66-68), paragraph for paragraph with the English; Code Explanation boxes and runnable examples added 2026-10-29.

blocks.text: Performance bottlenecks code ke woh hisse hain jo program ko sust karte hain. Profiling reports inhein dhoondne mein madad deti hain. Optimization ke tareeqon mein behtar algorithm, ghair zaroori kaam kam karna, ya achhe (efficient) data structures istemal karna shamil hai. Bottlenecks theek karne se poore program ki raftar aur jawab dene ki salahiyat (responsiveness) behtar hoti hai (Figure 5.4).

blocks.alt: Performance Test Cycle: chakkar Benchmark Run (oopar) se Bottleneck (daayein), Profile (neeche), Tuning (baayein) aur wapas. Lakeeron par: Verifying results, Fixing bottleneck, Collecting component characteristics, Collecting configuration. Andar aane wale teer: Refining tunings, Infrastructure, Profiling the application. Frame par Documentation components; Configuration - Network, CPU, Disks; Monitoring and profiling tool.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.4: Performance test ka chakkar (kitab ki Figure 5.4 ke mutabiq asal khaaka).

blocks.text:
import cProfile
import timeit


# Slow code example
def slow_sum(numbers):
    total = 0

    # Adding numbers one by one using a loop
    for num in numbers:
        total = total + num

    return total


# Fast code example
def fast_sum(numbers):
    # Python built-in sum() is faster and optimised
    return sum(numbers)


# Main function
def main():
    numbers = list(range(1, 1000000))

    print("Slow code result:", slow_sum(numbers))
    print("Fast code result:", fast_sum(numbers))


# Profiling the program using cProfile
print("Profiling Report:")
cProfile.run("main()")


# Comparing execution time using timeit
numbers = list(range(1, 1000000))

slow_time = timeit.timeit(lambda: slow_sum(numbers), number=10)
fast_time = timeit.timeit(lambda: fast_sum(numbers), number=10)

print("\nTime Comparison Report:")
print("Slow code time:", slow_time)
print("Fast code time:", fast_time)

items: cProfile profiling report banata hai jo dikhati hai ke program chalte waqt har function kitna waqt leta hai.
slow_sum() sust hai kyunke yeh loop se aik aik number khud jama karta hai.
fast_sum() tez hai kyunke yeh Python ka built-in sum() function istemal karta hai jo pehle se optimise hai.
Jo function zyada waqt le use bottleneck kehte hain.
timeit sust aur tez code ke waqt ka muqabla karne mein madad deta hai (har function 10 dafa chalta hai).

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"import cProfile" aur "import timeit": waqt napne wale do built-in modules.
"def slow_sum(numbers):": total = 0 se shuru kar ke for loop se har number aik aik kar ke jama karta hai.
"def fast_sum(numbers):": Python ka built-in sum() istemal karta hai jo andar se tez (optimised) hai.
"def main():": "numbers = list(range(1, 1000000))" 1 se 999,999 tak numbers ki list banata hai (range ka aakhri number shamil nahi hota) aur dono functions ka nateeja print karta hai.
"cProfile.run("main()")": main() chala kar report banata hai: har function kitni dafa chala (ncalls) aur kitna waqt laga (tottime = sirf apna waqt, cumtime = andar bulaye functions samet waqt).
"timeit.timeit(lambda: slow_sum(numbers), number=10)": slow_sum ko 10 dafa chala kar kul waqt seconds mein deta hai; isi tarah fast_sum. lambda aik chhota be-naam function hai.
"print("\nTime Comparison Report:")": \n pehle aik khaali line deta hai.
Output: pehle "Profiling Report:", phir "Slow code result: 499999500000" aur "Fast code result: 499999500000", phir cProfile ki table, phir "Time Comparison Report:" aur dono waqt. Asal cProfile table kitab se lambi hoti hai (maslan "25 function calls in 0.042 seconds" aur file ke naam aur line number ke saath functions), aur waqt har computer aur har run par alag hota hai. Phir bhi slow code ka waqt hamesha fast code se kai guna zyada aata hai (hamare run mein taqreeban 0.17 aur 0.04 second).
Khud try karein: range(1, 1000000) ko range(1, 100000) kar ke chalayein; dono waqt taqreeban das guna kam ho jayenge aur result 4999950000 hoga.

items: Dono functions aik hi nateeja dete hain: 499999500000 (1 se 999,999 tak ka jama).
slow_sum() zyada waqt leta hai kyunke is mein khud likha hua (manual) loop hai.
fast_sum() kam waqt leta hai kyunke yeh Python ka built-in sum() istemal karta hai.
Is liye is program mein slow_sum() bottleneck hai.

blocks.title: Asaan alfaaz mein
blocks.text: Kitab ka output sirf namoona hai: asal cProfile report mein zyada function calls aur lambi lines hoti hain (maslan {built-in method builtins.sum}), aur waqt har computer par alag hota hai. Kitab ke namoona run mein loop ne taqreeban 0.42 s aur sum() ne taqreeban 0.09 s liye.

blocks.caption: Kitab ke sample output ka waqt ka muwazna (hamara apna khaaka; kitab mein yeh figure nahi).

blocks.prompt: Aik program 5,000 talaba ke har jore ko do nested loops se jaanchta hai. Yeh kitne muwazne hain, aur yeh bottleneck kyun ho sakta hai?
blocks.explanation: 5,000 x 5,000 = 25,000,000 muwazne (har jora aik dafa jaanchein to taqreeban aadhe). Kaam talaba ki tadaad ke murabba ke saath barhta hai, is liye class dugni karne se yeh chaar guna sust hota hai; profiling dikhayegi ke zyada tar waqt yahi loop leta hai.

blocks.text: Bottleneck theek karne ki misal: list mein dohraye (duplicate) naam dhoondne ke do tareeqe. Nested loops har naam ko har doosre naam se milate hain; set (tez data structure) aik hi chakkar mein kaam kar deta hai. names ki list barha kar Run karein aur muwazne (comparisons) ginein.

names = ["Ali", "Sara", "Hina", "Ali", "Omar", "Sara"]   # in mein dohraye naam dhoondne hain

# Sust tareeqa: nested loops, har naam ko har agle naam se milao
comparisons = 0
slow_found = []
for i in range(len(names)):
    for j in range(i + 1, len(names)):
        comparisons = comparisons + 1
        if names[i] == names[j] and names[i] not in slow_found:
            slow_found.append(names[i])
print("Nested loops:", slow_found, "| muwazne:", comparisons)

# Tez tareeqa: set mein yaad rakho, aik hi chakkar
seen = set()
fast_found = []
steps = 0
for name in names:
    steps = steps + 1
    if name in seen and name not in fast_found:
        fast_found.append(name)
    seen.add(name)
print("Set ke saath:", fast_found, "| qadam:", steps)

blocks.title: Code Explanation (Wazahat)
blocks.text:
"names = [...]": chhe naam; Ali aur Sara do do dafa hain.
Sust tareeqa: do loops; "range(i + 1, len(names))" har naam ko sirf agle naamon se milata hai. Har muwazne par "comparisons" 1 barhta hai. Milte naam "slow_found" mein (aik dafa) jate hain.
Tez tareeqa: "seen = set()" dekhe hue naamon ka set. "if name in seen": naam pehle dekha ja chuka ho to woh dohraya hua hai. set mein dhoondna bohat tez hota hai, is liye sirf aik chakkar lagta hai.
Output: "Nested loops: ['Ali', 'Sara'] | muwazne: 15" aur "Set ke saath: ['Ali', 'Sara'] | qadam: 6". Jawab aik hi hai, magar kaam 15 ke muqable mein 6.
Khud try karein: list mein 4 aur naam jorein (kul 10): nested loops ke muwazne 45 ho jayenge, magar set ke qadam sirf 10. List jitni lambi, farq utna bara.

items: Bottleneck: program ko sust karne wala hissa.
Ilaj: behtar algorithm, kam ghair zaroori kaam, achhe data structures; phir dobara napein.
